plan.summary: A wording-only change: the five instruction texts that tell a worker what to write all carry one sentence saying retro's push never carries the `skip-checks: true` line, whatever paths it touches; three describing sentences tie the absence of checks to the line rather than to the paths; skills/legion-retro/SKILL.md gains the cure a retro worker can apply itself; packages/claude-envoy/legion/ is regenerated; packages/pi-legion/CHANGELOG.md records it; and one scratch pull request measures the two arms on GitHub. No daemon behaviour changes.
plan.canonicalSentence: Retro's push never carries the line, whatever paths it touches, because it is the last push before the merge and a base that requires a check will not merge a head whose checks never ran.
ordering: Task A, the live GitHub measurement, runs first: it needs no text and is the long pole (two full runs of the required checks, `test` 12-17 minutes).

Gate before any text edit: `gh pr view 2121 --repo sjawhar/legion --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit`. Not merged -> edit nothing, report to the architect with that reading, wait. #2121 creates skills/legion-worker/references/skip-checks-trailer.md and rewrites most of the same files, so a fix written against main's wording would be carried back out by the merge of the two.
Merged -> forward-merge main into legion/INFRA-149 per skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md (*Reintegrating the base*), never `jj rebase`.
Then Tasks B to F in one implementing round on top of that merge; recompute Task C's inventory and rebuild the mirror again if main moves under the branch.

liveProof.surface: a scratch pull request on sjawhar/legion, built in a throwaway clone outside $LEGION_WORKSPACE on a branch outside the `legion/` namespace (no ruleset there, read 2026-10-24; the daemon's push intake keys on legion/<KEY>)
liveProof.setup: work=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$work" && git -c credential.helper='!legion git-credential' -c credential.useHttpPath=true clone https://github.com/sjawhar/legion scratch && cd scratch && git checkout -b scratch/infra-149-skip-checks-proof origin/main
heads: head 0 (code): add scratch-infra-149-a.md and scratch-infra-149-b.md, one neutral line each; push; open the pull request with a title matching ^[a-z]+(\([^)]+\))?!?: .+
head 1: `git rm scratch-infra-149-a.md`, commit with no trailer, push, wait for the checks to settle before the next push

head 2: `git rm scratch-infra-149-b.md`, `git commit --cleanup=verbatim -m $'chore: delete the second scratch file


skip-checks: true'` (--cleanup=verbatim is required; git's default cleanup collapses the two empty lines), push
liveProof.negativeControl: head 1 against head 2: the same shape, one file deleted and nothing else, differing only by the line.
liveProof.discipline: Post no comment, review or body edit on the scratch pull request between the pushes and the readings: .github/workflows/pr-title.yaml runs on issue_comment, pull_request_review and pull_request_review_comment too, and any of them would put a pr-title run on the trailered head.
liveProof.teardown: the implementer closes it with `gh pr close` and leaves the branch; the tester re-reads both heads, then deletes the ref with `gh api --method DELETE repos/sjawhar/legion/git/refs/heads/scratch/infra-149-skip-checks-proof`. Never a pushed deletion from the shared clone.

testerWork: Re-read both scratch heads by SHA and judge the implementer's recorded readings; a closed pull request keeps refs/pull/<n>/head so both commits stay readable.
Delete the scratch ref and record it.
Re-run every acceptance command at the branch head, and the four guards.

Break-the-wording pass: for each of retro's four pushes (learnings and removal together, the removal alone, a re-push after a refused push, a rewritten head), judge whether any of the five texts or three sentences can still be read as asking for the line. Any yes is a failure recorded against the implementer.
Read CI on GitHub for the branch head; rerun no CI lane locally.
plan.invariant: No push carrying the line can be the commit that merges, because retro's push is always the last: learnings and removal together is a code push; the removal alone carries no line after this change; a retro with nothing to remove makes no commit (skills/legion-retro/SKILL.md:125-127) and the head stays at the earlier untrailered removal, which ran the checks. Any round after retro writes .legion/<issue>/ again and READY refuses that head (READY_HEAD_CARRIES_HANDOFFS), so the issue returns to retro.

skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md - the forward merge of main after #2121 lands is a step of this plan (*Reintegrating the base*), and *Rewriting pushed commits* is the section the new retro sentence points at, so the implementer must read it to describe the cure correctly.

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md - the implementer writes the body and its E2E (implementer) line, and this change's proof is a measurement rather than an application run, so the definition of a proof governs what it records.
skill://legion-retro/SKILL.md - two of the edits are inside it, and the implementer is the worker that runs retro, so it must read its own future instructions before rewording them.
skill://ce-simplify-code - the repository's simplify pass, once per pull request, in the first implementing round.
skill://dispatch - any write to the issue (the measurement's output goes on it).

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md - what the tester verifies, its E2E (tester) line, and the rule that lint, types and the unit suites are CI's work read on GitHub, which matters here because almost every check of this change is a guard CI already runs.
skill://dispatch - the readings go on the Dispatch issue.

findings.finding: The acceptance grep `grep -rn 'skip-checks\|trailer' skills/ packages/daemon/internal/prompts/` covers about three times the text the spec names (25 lines in 13 files), and two hits are a different sense of the word (the Omp-Session attribution trailer at skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md:166 and templates.commit_trailers in the recipe), so the criterion as written is false even after a perfect fix.
findings.answer: The plan ships the full 25-line disposition table (edited / unchanged with its reason / different word), has the implementer recompute the list after the forward merge and disposition every line in its handoff, and adds a literal grep of the canonical sentence per text as the machine-checkable criterion. Recorded as a spec departure.

findings.finding: Tying the absence of checks to the line rather than the paths would make packages/daemon/internal/prompts/go/architect-common.md:8 false about the daemon: classify/push.go:30-33 classifies a push handoff-only by path prefix alone, so the daemon still carries the code head's verdict across retro's deletion-only push, which now also has real check runs of its own.
findings.answer: Task C splits that sentence into two claims - GitHub starts no run for a head whose message carries the trailer; the daemon carries the verdict across any push that changes only `.legion/`, trailer or not - and the plan states the new consequence (retro's head has both a carried verdict and its own runs, whose red settles like any other). Recorded as a spec departure.

findings.finding: The spec states the failure as GitHub blocking while Legion reads green; on main today the daemon refuses the merger's READY with READY_CHECKS_NOT_GREEN instead.

findings.finding: The cure sentence has an unanswered branch (what retro does when the rewrite guard does not clear) and sits in the same skill as an absolute 'never force'.
findings.answer: Task D answers all three: a non-empty guard means do not rewrite and report the listed commits to the architect; the sentence says the rewritten head is a code head whose checks run from scratch and the merge waits; and it names the `--allow-backwards` bookmark move as the one the rewrite section sanctions, distinct from forcing a refused push.

findings.finding: The ordering against #2121 is unsafe for more than the two moving texts: it also rewrites merge-gate.md, the prompts, the guard test and the whole generated mirror, and a mirror rebuilt before the forward merge is stale by construction.
findings.answer: The plan makes the whole text change one atomic round after the gate and the forward merge, puts the mirror rebuild last, runs only the live measurement before the gate, and says what to redo if main moves mid-flight.

The criterion holds in the merged state; the plan adds the grep for it.

findings.finding: The invariant the fix rests on - retro's push is always the last before the merge - is asserted without naming the case where retro pushes nothing.
findings.answer: The plan states the invariant with all three cases, including the retro that has nothing to remove (skills/legion-retro/SKILL.md:125-127) and the round after retro that READY refuses with READY_HEAD_CARRIES_HANDOFFS.

specDepartures.spec: The live proof: 'GitHub runs the four checks the main branch requires on that head and reports the pull request mergeable.'
specDepartures.plan: The verdict is the check-run set at each head: four required checks completed/success on the untrailered head, an empty list on the trailered one. mergeable, mergeStateStatus and statusCheckRollup are recorded for both arms as context, not as the test, and no Legion role approves a scratch pull request.
specDepartures.evidence: `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/rules/branches/main` on 2026-10-24 returns a pull_request rule with required_approving_review_count 1, so an unapproved scratch pull request reads mergeStateStatus BLOCKED in both arms and mergeability separates nothing. dispatch://SMOKE-2/message/b5e12573-4767-4ca9-9c8b-11e6d76c375d recorded the same shape: a skip-checks head reads MERGEABLE/BLOCKED with an empty rollup.

acceptance: The live GitHub item's verdict becomes the two heads' check-run sets rather than the pull request's mergeability.

specDepartures.spec: 'The check is a search of the whole instruction surface ... `grep -rn 'skip-checks\|trailer' skills/ packages/daemon/internal/prompts/`: every hit either states that rule, or states one role's own push under it where that push is never the last before a merge, or ties the absence of checks to the line rather than to the paths.'
specDepartures.plan: The criterion becomes the same search with a published disposition for every line - edited, a role's own push that is never the last before a merge, a code push, already line-based, or a different word - recomputed after the forward merge, plus a literal grep of the canonical sentence in each of the five texts.
specDepartures.evidence: That search returns 25 lines in 13 files on main (read 2026-10-24). Two of them are a different sense of the word and can never state the rule: skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md:166 (the Omp-Session attribution trailer) and the recipe's `templates.commit_trailers=""`.

acceptance: The one-rule item is checked by a dispositioned inventory plus a literal per-text grep, not by every grep hit stating the rule.

specDepartures.spec: 'Three more sentences ... go from false to true with the same edit, because they tie the absence of checks to the paths a push touches instead of to the line ... each says instead that it is the line, not the paths, that stops them.'
specDepartures.plan: Two of the three are converted as the spec says. The third, packages/daemon/internal/prompts/go/architect-common.md:8, is split into two claims, because the same sentence also states the daemon's carry, which stays path-based.
specDepartures.evidence: packages/daemon/internal/classify/push.go:30-33 classifies a push handoff-only when every changed path starts `.legion/`, with no reading of the commit message, so after this change retro's deletion-only push both carries the code head's verdict and has check runs of its own.

acceptance: The third describing sentence states two claims - GitHub's runs follow the line, the daemon's carry follows the paths - rather than being converted whole to the line.
